Camera Control support just murdered all doubts. Dazz Cam now launches instantly and slots into the iPhone shooting workflow so naturally that Apple’s native Camera app suddenly feels like a dated relic.

This update turns Dazz Cam into a legitimate system-level camera replacement. It’s no longer just a pretty third-party app — it’s a real competitor that’s aggressively pushing the native Camera out of the way.
Extremely strong work. Respect. 🔥

title: Such a fun app
content:
I've had this app for a few years now and I absolutely love it. The developers are great, they constantly update the app with new features. Honestly I thought this might be similar to some other disposable camera apps where they never really change it but they updated it to match a liquid glass and that's just one example of a time I was blown away by the constant support and update updates they make to the app.  

The great thing is you don't need to pay for it to get a great experience, I did not pay for it for the first two years and I loved it. But then I finally bit the bullet and paid for premium and honestly I think it's worth it too. You get way more filters and it also just feels good to support the developers of an app you're passionate about. Love this app so much i always use it at parties and special events and people were blown away by how cute the photos look! However just a tip for you guys go into settings and make sure you have it save the original photo to your camera roll as well as the edited photo, this will help you make sure you cover your bases in case someone doesn't like the photo that you just took. This is also great because you can go to a party and tell someone "hey let's use my app"
 and then you take the edited version of the photo with their filter, but you also have the original version, and you can send both to your friends, just in case they don't like to edit. I honestly love this so much because it's the best of both worlds and my friends love it too. Have fun!!

title: I paid the $20 but now regret it
content:
I paid the $20 because genuinely 10/10 fantastic as-advertised quality.

But regret it now because the UX has not been thought out properly and that actively gets in the way of the very function and purpose of this app!

There are too many options and the tap targets are way too small and it is unnecessarily difficult to see preview samples for each camera (am I expected to memorize all of them?!) robbing the moment from joy.

This should feel as ergonomically tight and defined as a real camera at $20 rather than an “app” with carousel-style UI.

Please change your design philosophy behind the UX to make it more of a “ready-to-go vintage camera in the user’s pocket with extremely intelligent and efficient workflows and UX flows for uninterrupted joyful use and experimentation” vs “an iOS app offering filters for the camera”
